slides.title: Core Mitigation Techniques
points: Mitigation techniques reduce attack surface, contain compromise, enforce secure access, and keep systems resilient.

slides.title: Segmentation
slides.teach: Divides networks, systems, or environments into separate zones to limit communication and reduce lateral movement.

course.learn: Divides networks, systems, or environments into separate zones to limit communication and reduce lateral movement.

breakdown.explanation: Break the environment into controlled sections so one compromise does not spread everywhere.
VLAN segmentation, DMZ, Microsegmentation

course.why: It limits blast radius and makes lateral movement harder.
course.example: Guest Wi-Fi is isolated from finance systems.
course.check_q: What does Segmentation mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Divides networks, systems, or environments into separate zones to limit communication and reduce lateral movement.

slides.title: Access Control
slides.teach: Restricts who or what can access resources.

course.learn: Restricts who or what can access resources.

breakdown.explanation: Decide who gets access and under what conditions.
Role-based access, Network access rules

course.why: It reduces unauthorized use of systems and data.
course.example: Only HR staff can open payroll records.
course.check_q: What does Access Control mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Restricts who or what can access resources.

slides.title: Access Control List (ACL)
slides.teach: A rule set that permits or denies traffic or access based on defined criteria.

course.learn: A rule set that permits or denies traffic or access based on defined criteria.

breakdown.explanation: A list of explicit allow/deny rules.
Router ACL, File ACL

course.example: A router ACL blocks traffic from an untrusted subnet.
course.check_q: What does Access Control List (ACL) mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: A rule set that permits or denies traffic or access based on defined criteria.

slides.title: Permissions
slides.teach: Specific rights assigned to users, groups, or processes for resources.

course.learn: Specific rights assigned to users, groups, or processes for resources.

breakdown.explanation: They define what an authorized subject can actually do.
Read, Write, Execute

course.why: They limit actions even after access is granted.
course.example: A user can read a file but cannot modify it.
course.check_q: What does Permissions mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Specific rights assigned to users, groups, or processes for resources.

slides.title: Application Allow List
slides.teach: Permits only approved applications to execute.

course.learn: Permits only approved applications to execute.

breakdown.explanation: Only software on the approved list can run.
Only signed business apps allowed

course.why: It blocks unknown or unauthorized executables.
course.exam: Only approved apps run → APPLICATION ALLOW LIST.
course.check_q: What does Application Allow List mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Permits only approved applications to execute.

slides.title: Isolation
slides.teach: Separates a system, device, process, or workload from others to contain risk.

course.learn: Separates a system, device, process, or workload from others to contain risk.

breakdown.explanation: Keep the suspicious or risky thing separate.
Quarantine endpoint, Sandbox process

course.why: It limits communication and prevents spread.
course.check_q: What does Isolation mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Separates a system, device, process, or workload from others to contain risk.

slides.title: Patching
slides.teach: Applies vendor fixes to correct vulnerabilities and software defects.

course.learn: Applies vendor fixes to correct vulnerabilities and software defects.

breakdown.explanation: Install the update that fixes the known flaw.
OS update, Application security patch

course.example: A critical browser CVE is fixed with a vendor patch.
course.check_q: What does Patching mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Applies vendor fixes to correct vulnerabilities and software defects.

slides.title: Encryption
slides.teach: Protects confidentiality by converting readable data into ciphertext.

course.learn: Protects confidentiality by converting readable data into ciphertext.

breakdown.explanation: Make data unreadable without the proper key.
Disk encryption, TLS

course.why: It reduces exposure if data is stolen or intercepted.
course.example: A stolen laptop's data remains unreadable.
course.check_q: What does Encryption mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Protects confidentiality by converting readable data into ciphertext.

slides.title: Monitoring
slides.teach: Observes systems, logs, traffic, and behavior for suspicious or abnormal activity.

course.learn: Observes systems, logs, traffic, and behavior for suspicious or abnormal activity.

breakdown.explanation: Watch the environment for signs of trouble.
SIEM alerts, Network monitoring

course.why: It improves detection and response speed.
course.example: A SIEM alerts on unusual admin logins.
course.check_q: What does Monitoring mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Observes systems, logs, traffic, and behavior for suspicious or abnormal activity.

slides.title: Least Privilege
slides.teach: Grants only the minimum permissions necessary to perform a task.

course.learn: Grants only the minimum permissions necessary to perform a task.

breakdown.explanation: Give users and services no more access than they need.
Standard user instead of admin, Restricted service account

course.why: It reduces damage if an account is misused or compromised.
course.example: A help-desk user loses unnecessary domain-admin rights.
course.check_q: What does Least Privilege mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Grants only the minimum permissions necessary to perform a task.

slides.title: Configuration Enforcement
slides.teach: Ensures systems remain aligned with approved secure settings and baselines.

course.learn: Ensures systems remain aligned with approved secure settings and baselines.

breakdown.explanation: Keep devices from drifting away from secure configuration.
MDM policy, Configuration baseline

course.example: MDM re-enables a required security control after a user disables it.
course.exam: System drifts from baseline → CONFIGURATION ENFORCEMENT.
course.check_q: What does Configuration Enforcement mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Ensures systems remain aligned with approved secure settings and baselines.

blocks.title: Core Mitigation Techniques exam shortcuts
items: Example: Finance is isolated from guest Wi-Fi.
Only approved apps run → APPLICATION ALLOW LIST
Execution is limited to approved software.
Separate the device from normal communications.
Example: EDR quarantines an infected laptop.
Apply the update that removes the flaw.
Example: A critical CVE is patched.
Reduce rights to only what is needed.
Example: Unneeded admin rights are removed.
blocks.example: Focus on the risk first, then choose the control that directly reduces it.

questions.q: Guest Wi-Fi is separated from finance systems so a compromised guest device cannot reach internal servers. Which mitigation is best?
questions.explanation: Segmentation limits communication between zones and reduces lateral movement.

questions.q: A router explicitly permits HTTPS from one subnet and denies other inbound traffic. Which control is this?
questions.explanation: An ACL uses explicit permit/deny rules.

questions.q: A user can read a file but cannot modify or delete it. Which control is most direct?
questions.explanation: Permissions define allowed actions such as read and write.

questions.q: Only approved signed applications may execute on endpoints. Which mitigation is this?
questions.explanation: Application allowlisting permits only approved software to run.

questions.q: EDR quarantines an infected laptop from the corporate network. Which mitigation is this?
A vendor releases a fix for a critical vulnerability and administrators deploy it. Which mitigation is this?
questions.explanation: Patching applies vendor fixes to known vulnerabilities.

questions.q: A help-desk technician has unnecessary administrator rights removed. Which principle is being applied?
questions.explanation: Least privilege grants only the access required.

questions.q: MDM automatically restores required security settings after users change them. Which mitigation is this?
questions.explanation: Configuration enforcement maintains approved secure baselines.
